9: /// ## What it does
10: /// Checks for `for` loops that can be replaced with `yield from` expressions.
11: ///
12: /// ## Why is this bad?
13: /// If a `for` loop only contains a `yield` statement, it can be replaced with a
14: /// `yield from` expression, which is more concise and idiomatic.
15: ///
16: /// ## Example
17: /// ```python
18: /// for x in foo:
19: ///     yield x
20: /// ```
21: ///
22: /// Use instead:
23: /// ```python
24: /// yield from foo
25: /// ```
26: ///
27: /// ## Fix safety
28: /// This rule's fix is marked as unsafe, as converting a `for` loop to a `yield
29: /// from` expression can change the behavior of the program in rare cases.
30: /// For example, if a generator is being sent values via `send`, then rewriting
31: /// to a `yield from` could lead to an attribute error if the underlying
32: /// generator does not implement the `send` method.
33: ///
34: /// In most cases, however, the fix is safe, and such a modification should have
35: /// no effect on the behavior of the program.
36: ///
37: /// ## References
38: /// - [Python documentation: The `yield` statement](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/simple_stmts.html#the-yield-statement)
39: /// - [PEP 380 – Syntax for Delegating to a Subgenerator](https://peps.python.org/pep-0380/)
40: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
41: pub(crate) struct YieldInForLoop;
42: 
43: impl AlwaysFixableViolation for YieldInForLoop {
44:     #[derive_message_formats]
45:     fn message(&self) -> String {
46:         "Replace `yield` over `for` loop with `yield from`".to_string()
47:     }
48: 
49:     fn fix_title(&self) -> String {
50:         "Replace with `yield from`".to_string()
51:     }
52: }

54: /// Candidate `for` loop whose target and iterable can be rewritten to `yield from`.
55: pub(crate) struct YieldFromForLoop<'a> {
56:     target: &'a Expr,
57:     iter: &'a Expr,
58: }
59: 
60: impl<'a> YieldFromForLoop<'a> {
61:     pub(crate) fn new(stmt_for: &'a ast::StmtFor) -> Self {
62:         Self {
63:             target: stmt_for.target.as_ref(),
64:             iter: stmt_for.iter.as_ref(),
65:         }
66:     }
67: 
68:     /// UP028
69:     pub(crate) fn yield_in_for_loop(&self, checker: &mut Checker, stmt_for: &ast::StmtFor) {
70:         // Intentionally omit async contexts.
71:         if checker.semantic().in_async_context() {
72:             return;
73:         }
74: 
75:         let ast::StmtFor {
76:             target: _,
77:             iter: _,
78:             body,
79:             orelse,
80:             is_async: _,
81:             range: _,
82:         } = stmt_for;
83: 
84:         // If there is an else statement, don't rewrite.
85:         if !orelse.is_empty() {
86:             return;
87:         }
88: 
89:         // If there's any logic besides a yield, don't rewrite.
90:         let [body] = body.as_slice() else {
91:             return;
92:         };
93: 
94:         // If the body is not a yield, don't rewrite.
95:         let Stmt::Expr(ast::StmtExpr { value, range: _ }) = &body else {
96:             return;
97:         };
98:         let Expr::Yield(ast::ExprYield {
99:             value: Some(value),
100:             range: _,
101:         }) = value.as_ref()
102:         else {
103:             return;
104:         };
105: 
106:         // If the target is not the same as the value, don't rewrite. For example, we should rewrite
107:         // `for x in y: yield x` to `yield from y`, but not `for x in y: yield x + 1`.
108:         if !is_same_expr(self.target, value) {
109:             return;
110:         }
111: 
112:         // If any of the bound names are used outside of the yield itself, don't rewrite.
113:         if collect_names(value).any(|name| {
114:             checker
115:                 .semantic()
116:                 .current_scope()
117:                 .get_all(name.id.as_str())
118:                 // Skip unbound bindings like `del x`
119:                 .find(|&id| !checker.semantic().binding(id).is_unbound())
120:                 .is_some_and(|binding_id| {
121:                     let binding = checker.semantic().binding(binding_id);
122:                     binding.references.iter().any(|reference_id| {
123:                         checker.semantic().reference(*reference_id).range() != name.range()
124:                     })
125:                 })
126:         }) {
127:             return;
128:         }
129: 
130:         let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(YieldInForLoop, stmt_for.range());
131:         let contents = checker.locator().slice(
132:             parenthesized_range(
133:                 self.iter.into(),
134:                 stmt_for.into(),
135:                 checker.comment_ranges(),
136:                 checker.locator().contents(),
137:             )
138:             .unwrap_or(self.iter.range()),
139:         );
140:         let contents = format!("yield from {contents}");
141:         diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::unsafe_edit(Edit::range_replacement(
142:             contents,
143:             stmt_for.range(),
144:         )));
145:         checker.diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
146:     }
147: }

149: /// Return `true` if the two expressions are equivalent, and both consistent solely
150: /// of tuples and names.
151: fn is_same_expr(left: &Expr, right: &Expr) -> bool {
152:     match (&left, &right) {
153:         (Expr::Name(left), Expr::Name(right)) => left.id == right.id,
154:         (Expr::Tuple(left), Expr::Tuple(right)) => {
155:             left.len() == right.len()
156:                 && left
157:                     .iter()
158:                     .zip(right)
159:                     .all(|(left, right)| is_same_expr(left, right))
160:         }
161:         _ => false,
162:     }
163: }
164: 
165: /// Collect all named variables in an expression consisting solely of tuples and
166: /// names.
167: fn collect_names<'a>(expr: &'a Expr) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = &'a ast::ExprName> + 'a> {
168:     Box::new(
169:         expr.as_name_expr().into_iter().chain(
170:             expr.as_tuple_expr()
171:                 .into_iter()
172:                 .flat_map(|tuple| tuple.iter().flat_map(collect_names)),
173:         ),
174:     )
175: }
